bib.title: DocLLM: A Layout-Aware Generative Language Model for Multimodal Document Understanding

question: Can a text LLM be extended with only OCR bounding-box information, no image encoder, to understand visually rich documents?
hypothesis: Treating spatial layout as a separate modality via disentangled attention, plus block infilling pretraining, suffices for document intelligence tasks.
contributions: A light-weight extension to LLMs designed for understanding visual documents.
A disentangled spatial attention mechanism that captures cross-alignment between text and layout modalities.
An infilling pre-training objective tailored to address irregular layouts effectively.
An instruction-tuning dataset specially curated towards visual document intelligence tasks.
Comprehensive experiments and valuable insights into the model behavior.

method.summary: Falcon-1B and Llama2-7B are extended with disentangled text/spatial attention over OCR bounding boxes, pretrained with block infilling on 3.8B tokens of CDIP and DocBank, then instruction-tuned on 16 DocAI datasets (VQA, NLI, KIE, CLS). Evaluated in same-dataset (SDDS) and held-out-dataset (STDD) settings.
method.task: document VQA, NLI, key information extraction, document classification

datasets.name: IIT-CDIP Test Collection 1.0 + DocBank
datasets.source: CDIP: 1990s tobacco litigation documents; DocBank: layout analysis benchmark
datasets.preprocessing: OCR text with bounding boxes; OCR blocks used for block-level masking only during pretraining

datasets.name: Instruction-tuning mix (16 datasets: DocVQA, WTQ, VisualMRC, DUDE, BizDocs, TabFact, KLC, CORD, FUNSD, DeepForm, PWC, SROIE, VRDU ad-buy, RVL-CDIP)
datasets.split: unseen test split, or dev when no test; VRDU ad-buy random train-test split
datasets.source: public datasets; BizDocs is internal, due to be released
datasets.preprocessing: templated prompts; MCQ choices flattened into copies in train only; KIE test keeps extraction template only; CLS test keeps MCQ only; RVL-CDIP downsampled in train

datasets.name: STDD held-out: DocVQA, KLC, BizDocs
datasets.split: tuned on 11 of 16 datasets, tested on 3 held-out (5 dataset-task settings)

models.name: DocLLM-1B
models.architecture: causal decoder with disentangled spatial attention

models.name: DocLLM-7B
models.architecture: causal decoder with disentangled spatial attention

other.note: stated 36 layers although Llama2-7B has 32; as printed

training.objective: Pretrain: autoregressive block infilling (cross-entropy L_IF over masked OCR blocks, replaced by [M], conditioned with [S], output ends with [E]); instruction tuning: supervised on templated prompts
training.hardware: 7B: 8x 24GB A10g, FSDP via accelerate; 1B: single 24GB A10g

other.lambda: lambda_ss=1, lambda_st=0, lambda_ts=0 for all Sec 4 experiments
other.spatial_encoding: bounding boxes (left, top, right, bottom) encoded to hidden vectors S, reused across layers, per-layer Ws,q Ws,k projections; encoder of boxes not specified in detail

inference.prompting: Instruction templates (Table 1) with {document} = OCR text plus bounding boxes; baselines are zero-shot with OCR text only; zero-shot prompts refined by three prompt engineers, five rounds each, best of three groups taken, plus post-processing

metrics.name: ANLS
metrics.definition: Average Normalized Levenshtein Similarity, for VQA (DocVQA, DUDE, BizDocs)

metrics.name: NTP accuracy
metrics.definition: out-of-sample next-token prediction accuracy at pretraining, ablations only

eval.protocol: Single run; no seeds or significance tests stated. SDDS and STDD settings; ablations on 100,000 pretraining chunks, 1,000 unseen documents.

availability.data: BizDocs 'due to be released publicly'; others public

prompts.text: {document} What is the value for the "{key}"?
{document} What is "{value}" in the document? Possible choices: {choices}.
{document} What type of document is this? Possible choices: {choices}.
{document} What type of document is this?

results.note: Abstract says 'outperforms SotA LLMs on 14 out of 16 datasets'; Sec 4.3 says it excels in 12 of 16 when GPT-4 is included.
results.quote: Among equivalent models (excluding GPT4), our model outperforms in 14 out of 16 datasets.

results.claim: Including GPT-4, DocLLM-7B is best on 12 of 16 datasets.
results.quote: we observe that DocLLM-7B excels in 12 out of 16 datasets

results.claim: DocLLM-7B on DocVQA (ANLS) vs GPT-4+OCR zero-shot: GPT-4 is higher.
results.setup: SDDS, DocLLM-7B instruction-tuned, GPT-4 ZS with OCR text.

results.claim: Intro claims 15% to 61% improvement over Llama2-7B in four of five unseen datasets.
results.quote: result in a performance improvement ranging from 15% to 61% for the Llama2-7B model in four out of five previously unseen datasets

results.claim: Ablation: text-only attention gives lowest NTP accuracy; spatial-to-spatial only (lambda_ss=1) plus T2T is highest.
results.setup: Pre-training subset: 100,000 chunks, 1,000 unseen test documents, NTP out-of-sample accuracy.

results.claim: Ablation: block infilling + spatial beats causal learning.
results.note: Causal + Spatial = 36.2; so spatial adds 3.6 points, infilling a further 2.9

results.claim: Causal decoder is marginally better than prefix decoder, so causal is used.
results.note: Numbers only in Fig 4, not in text.
results.quote: with the causal decoder having a slight edge over the prefix

results.claim: Higher weight decay (0.1 vs 0.01), higher instruction-tuning lr (1e-4 vs 5e-5) and cosine scheduler tend to help.
results.setup: Informal internal experience; authors acknowledge absence of robust validation.
results.quote: we observe that a higher weight decay (e.g., 0.1 versus 0.01) generally improves performance

limits: No vision: OCR quality bounds performance; OCR engines/layout parsers not compared (future work).
STDD only three held-out datasets because of instruction-tuning cost; CLS generalises poorly (single classification training dataset).
Training insights (weight decay, lr, scheduler) given without robust validation.
7B instruct-tuned only 3 epochs vs 10 for 1B due to compute; context 1,024 only.
Baselines are zero-shot with OCR text only; DocLLM is instruction-tuned, so comparison is not like-for-like; no seeds or variance.
Ablations use NTP accuracy on a small pretraining subset, not downstream metrics.
Instruction-tuning data crowdsourced instructions/preferences left to future work; BizDocs internal.
